d_sv_content.name: Dual Energy CT to Assess Bone Mineral Density in Dogs with Osteosarcoma Undergoing Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us study how radiation and chemotherapy affect bone health in dogs with bone cancer.
d_sv_content.description: This study looks at how bones change in dogs with bone cancer in the leg (called osteosarcoma) after radiation treatment. Veterinarians and researchers will test blood and urine to see how much bone is breaking down before and after a special type of radiation treatment called SBRT (stereotactic body radiation therapy). They will compare this information to bone strength, how well the treatment works, and the risk of the bone breaking.
d_sv_content.requirements: A special CT scan (dual energy CT) to plan radiation treatment3 daily SBRT radiation treatmentsChemotherapy with a drug called carboplatin:First dose given at the last radiation treatment5 more doses given every 3 weeksBlood and urine samples collected:Before treatment2 weeks after the first chemotherapy doseAt every other chemotherapy visitA follow-up CT scan at the final chemotherapy visitAfter chemotherapy, visits every 8 weeks for chest X-rays and blood and urine samples
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Schedule and attend all treatment and study appointmentsPay for:The first exam and tests to diagnose the cancerThe CT scan done before treatmentAll radiation (SBRT) and chemotherapy treatmentsChest X-raysAny care needed for side effects from radiation or chemotherapy
d_sv_content.whoCan: Dogs may join the study if they:Have confirmed osteosarcoma in a legWill receive SBRT radiation followed by carboplatin chemotherapyDo not have a broken bone caused by the cancerDo not have cancer spread to other areasHave never had radiation treatmentHave not had chemotherapy in the past 30 daysCan come to CSU for all study visits
d_sv_content.benefits: Benefits:Helps improve understanding of bone health during cancer treatmentThe study will pay for:The follow-up CT scan and anesthesia recoveryAll blood and urine collections for the studyTests that measures bone breakdownFunds are available to pay for screening tests to determine eligibility, including blood tests, imaging of the chest, and tumor sampling   Risks:The study involves additional CT scans and blood/urine collections, which may be stressful for some dogsThere is a risk of side effects from radiation therapy and carboplatin chemotherapy
d_sv_content.compensation: The study will pay for: follow-up CT scan, all blood and urine collections for the study, tests. The study will also contribute $1500 towards the cost of SBRT which is charged at a discounted rate ($2500).
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: Dual energy CT for 3 SBRT treatments.  5 subsequent doses of chemotherapy  every 3 weeks. Post-chemo, dogs will return every 8 weeks for chest x-rays and sample collection.
